title: The Funk Bass
brief: Make a clean, played bass note whose tone opens on the attack and settles as it's held -- a filter "wah" under your fingers, not a fixed tone. Herbie Hancock's 1973 album Head Hunters (the track "Chameleon") put exactly this kind of synth-bass wah in a jazz musician's hands and argued that synthesis and improvisation weren't opposed -- a controversial move at the time, and a commercial hit anyway. Same four modules and the same envelope-reused-twice trick as the last couple of levels -- VCO -> VCF -> VCA -> Output, ADSR's "Out" into both the VCA's "CV" and the VCF's "CV" -- but tuned differently: keep the VCF's Res knob low (this is a clean wah, not a squeal), give the envelope a moderate Attack and enough Sustain that the note feels held and played rather than plucked and gone.
